acme-cs: Hey team — we're seeing weird behavior on /v1/embeddings. Intermittent vector dim mismatches (sometimes 1536, sometimes 1024) and a large number of cache MISSes. Latency jumps to ~1.2s under our usual load. Billing spiked overnight too. Repro steps below, pls advise.

elaine: sorry about that — can you paste the exact request (model + payload) and the prefix you pass to cache? Also any trace IDs would help.

acme-cs: Model: text-embedding-3-small. We batch at 128, send parallel clients (8 workers). Our code sets cache key prefix = "acme_prod" and we include the model name but not the model commit hash. Example request:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/inference/v1/embeddings \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":["..."],"cache_prefix":"acme_prod"}'
```
We started seeing this after a backend model swap yesterday.

kevin: thanks. Two quick hypotheses: (1) you may be reusing the same prefix across two different model variants/quantization profiles -> cache may return vectors of different dims, or cause collision-based misses, (2) batching + parallel clients may be producing out-of-order cache writes if your keying isn't per-item. Can you share a trace id?

acme-cs: trace: trace-0a1b2c3d, recent response sample: `{"embedding": [ ... length:1024 ...]}` but older responses were 1536.

mike: infra-bot logs show a burst of writes to the embeddings-prefetch cache for tenant "acme" at 2024-11-01T03:12:14Z. Also a couple of 429s from our cache layer indicating throttled writes. Looks like a simultaneous deploy + heavy prefetch job.

kevin: nailed it — the backend model swap introduced a new quantized build with dim=1024. Your cache prefix `acme_prod` is tenant-wide and doesn't include model_version. That means old entries (1536) are considered the same keyspace as new ones. When the runtime serves the new model it hits an old key and returns mismatched dims or misses depending on key format.

elaine: immediate mitigation options:
- change your cache_prefix to include the model version/hash (e.g., `acme_prod:v1.2:sha256(...)`)
- disable client-side prefetching until we confirm stable model rollout
- we can also temporarily set your tenant's cache TTL=0 to force cold misses while we reconcile entries
Which would you like us to do now?

acme-cs: please set TTL=0 for now and we'll update our prefix. Also curious about the billing spike — why billed for both old and new requests?

billing-bot: Alert: tenant acme experienced a 3x increase in embedding compute between 2024-11-01 02:00-04:00 UTC. An invoice notification was sent to billing@acme.com.

mike: TTL=0 applied for tenant "acme" (action id act-789). That will keep future requests from reading stale cached vectors. We're also throttling concurrent prefetch jobs for that tenant.

kevin: recommended prefix pattern and repro script (run locally to verify):
```python
PREFIX = f"acme_prod:{MODEL}:{MODEL_COMMIT[:8]}"
# ensure per-item keys include index/hash
for i, item in enumerate(batch):
    key = f"{PREFIX}:item:{sha256(item)[:12]}"
    cache.get_or_set(key, compute_embedding(item))
```
This avoids cross-version collisions and is safe for parallel writers.

acme-cs: switched to `acme_prod:text-embedding-3-small:commit-9f1a` and retried. Cache hit-rate jumped to ~95% and vector dims stable at 1024. Latency back to ~120ms. Billing seems to have normalized.

elaine: great — we'll keep TTL=0 for an hour then revert once you confirm steady state. We'll also add a KB article explaining safe prefix patterns and we will surface model_version in the SDK to prevent this class of bugs.

acme-cs: thanks, huge help. One follow-up: can you add a server-side guard so cached vector dim is validated before returning? We accidentally decoded a mismatched dim which caused downstream failures.

kevin: good suggestion — creating feature ticket to add dim validation + fallback. Filed RFC: INF-4721.

infra-bot: created incident INC-1234 for embedding-cache model-version collisions and linked RFC INF-4721.

elaine: closing thread for now, will follow up with postmortem and KB link. :thumbsup:
